subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or documented current limits with plugin workarounds?
rationale: Default backup exclusions can affect restore completeness and sensitive data handling, and the active implementation proposal adds new CLI/API surface with known compatibility and security-boundary concerns.

options.title: Review native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade/security review.

options.title: Ship reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress and size guidance while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader native exclude-pattern tracker.

options.title: Defer core expansion
options.body: Document current native backup limits and point users to plugin or ClawHub options such as KeepMyClaw if maintainers decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Review native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the current backup infra extraction and earlier backup CLI review, making them the strongest routing candidate for the restore-safety policy choice.
